I am 58 years old, a woman farmer in Quzhou County, Hebei. I finished middle school and have farmed these fields for 40 years. My household has two people — my husband works off‑farm at a construction site in the county town, so most days it is just me out there. We have 6 mu of flat land and a well for irrigation. I grow wheat in winter and corn in summer, wheat‑maize rotation, same as everyone around here.

I never start from nothing. I start from what I did last year, and last year was fine. For my 6 mu of winter wheat, I will put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer before sowing — that is one full bag for each mu, the 15‑15‑15 kind I buy from the dealer in town. Then at jointing time in late March, I will spread 25 kg of urea per mu, that is half a bag. I irrigate three times: the overwintering water before the deep cold, the jointing water when the wheat starts growing fast, and one more at grain filling in May. I spray twice — herbicide once when the weeds are small, and once for aphids or powdery mildew when it heads. After the corn comes off in late September, I rotary till the ground to make a flat seedbed for the wheat drill. I plant an improved wheat variety, not old local seed. Last year I got 500 kg per mu, and I expect about the same this year if the weather is normal.

For summer corn, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June. I have maybe one week, so I use the no‑till seeder and plant directly into the wheat stubble — no time to plow, and besides, everyone around here does it this way now. I buy hybrid seed, about 3 kg per mu, the dealer says it is Zhengdan 958 or something similar, I do not remember the exact number but it is the yellow bag. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the furrow at sowing, and at big trumpet stage I spread 25 kg urea per mu. Two irrigations: one right after sowing if the soil is dry, and the big trumpet water in July. The summer rains usually help. I spray herbicide once at seedling stage and insecticide once for corn borer. My neighbor Lao Wang got 600 kg per mu with the same seed and fertilizer last year, so I expect 600 kg per mu.

Six mu is not a big farm, and fertilizer is expensive now — urea went up again. But I would rather use a little too much than too little. If I waste 20 yuan on fertilizer, that is nothing. If I lose yield, that is a disaster. I have to pay for my husband's medicine and our daily costs. So I copy what works, I watch my neighbors, and I do not gamble.
